The core mechanism posits that vacuum stability (<1e-7 mbar) and seismic isolation (<1e-9 m/√Hz at 10 Hz) define the noise floor. We will generate synthetic gravitational wave strain data containing injected non-GR signals (specifically scalar-tensor theory dipole radiation terms) into a noise model parameterized by ET-PF technical specs. The study varies vacuum pressure and seismic noise parameters to determine the minimum detectable deviation amplitude (SNR threshold) for these non-GR features. If the noise floor exceeds the signal amplitude of predicted GR deviations, the hypothesis holds that technological limits constrain falsifiability.

experiment_design.methods:
1. Noise Modeling: Construct a frequency-domain noise PSD model for ET-PF. Key parameters include residual gas noise (dependent on vacuum pressure P) and seismic noise (dependent on isolation transfer function T(f)). 
2. Signal Injection: Generate waveform templates h(t) for binary black hole mergers using standard GR plus a scalar-tensor deviation term (e.g., dipole radiation amplitude proportional to coupling constant alpha). 
3. Matched Filtering: Perform matched filtering of injected signals against the noise-weighted template bank. 
4. Sensitivity Mapping: Vary P and T(f) systematically to map the detection threshold (SNR > 8) for the non-GR component as a function of instrumental performance. 
5. Falsifiability Boundary Definition: Identify the region in (P, T(f)) space where non-GR signals become undetectable, defining the 'technological lower bound'.

baselines: Standard GR Waveform Only: Inject pure GR signals to verify baseline detector sensitivity and ensure no false positives for non-GR terms.

Idealized Noise Floor: Use theoretical best-case noise curves (zero vacuum/seismic contribution) to establish the absolute physical limit of detectability, independent of ET-PF engineering constraints.
Current LIGO/Virgo Sensitivity: Use current ground-based detector noise curves as a comparative baseline to demonstrate the improvement required for strong-field tests.
metrics: Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of Non-GR Component: The primary metric for detectability of the deviation term.
Parameter Estimation Bias: Difference between injected and recovered scalar-tensor coupling constants.
False Alarm Rate (FAR): Rate at which pure GR signals are incorrectly identified as having non-GR components due to noise fluctuations.
Detection Efficiency: Fraction of injected non-GR signals recovered with SNR > threshold across multiple noise realizations.
ablation: Vacuum Noise Only: Fix seismic noise at ideal levels and vary vacuum pressure to isolate its impact on high-frequency sensitivity.
Seismic Noise Only: Fix vacuum pressure at ideal levels and vary seismic isolation performance to isolate its impact on low-frequency (<100 Hz) sensitivity.
Waveform Systematics: Test robustness against uncertainties in astrophysical parameters (mass, spin) to ensure non-detection is due to noise, not modeling errors.

Validate the noise model against public ET-PF design documents (EV-Q059-3afd01dc41fac1703fc69726) to ensure parameter ranges are physically plausible.
